heading: What We Do at CIReN
intro: CIReN builds the structures that let African university students do serious research and serious engineering. We run societies on campus, we put on the events where that work gets tested and seen, and we connect both to the people and opportunities that can take them further.
societiesIntro: Two standing communities, hosted on partner campuses.

societies.name: Researchers Society
societies.teaser: Research methodology, mentorship, and a route to global conferences.
societies.description: We train young researchers to understand research methodologies and connect them with the opportunities around the globe. We work on research projects that can be showcased at research conferences.

societies.name: Innovators Society
societies.teaser: Build alongside strong engineers in software, AI and applied ML.
societies.description: An innovators club where young innovators find themselves surrounded by strong builders they can learn, collaborate and solve problems with — through software engineering, AI and applied machine learning.

eventsIntro: Where the work gets built, tested and presented.

events.name: Hackathons & Build Events
events.description: We organise hackathons by sourcing corporate support to bring the spirit of innovation and problem solving across universities and college communities.

events.name: Research Conferences
events.teaser: A stage for young researchers to present their work.
events.description: We organise research conferences to allow young researchers present their works to faculties, industry experts, other researchers, and all those who could transform the world with the research these young researchers produce.

inspiration.heading: What inspired our work?
inspiration.blurb: CIReN did not start from an idea. It started from a case study, and from the research paper that came out of it.

caseStudy.title: The Case Study Behind CIReN
body: Every organisation that lasts starts from a question somebody could not stop asking. Ours began on a campus, in a lab that had the people but not the pathway.

The students were capable. The supervision was willing. What was missing was the connective tissue between a good idea and the machinery that turns a good idea into published, cited, funded work: the methodology, the mentors who had done it before, the compute, and the rooms where the work gets shown.

We spent a year watching where projects stalled. They rarely stalled for lack of talent. They stalled at the handoffs — between an idea and a method, between a draft and a reviewer, between a finished result and an audience who could act on it.
That pattern repeated across every campus we looked at, which is what told us it was structural rather than local. A structural problem can be designed against.

CIReN is that design. The societies supply the method and the peers. The hackathons and conferences supply the deadline and the audience. The network supplies everything that a single campus cannot hold on its own.
